transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-04-11 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 47m
Attendees: Alyssa Kim (Redwood AE), Diego Marquez (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Novara - Head of Data), Evan Zhou (Novara - Platform Eng), Marta Lopez (Novara - Compliance), Tom (Novara - Sourcing)

Summary:
Quick demo of Redwood Console Privacy Configurator and the API sandbox flags (store toggles, redaction presets). Customer wants to validate store=false flows, audit log retention, and KMS integration for PII at rest. Agreed next steps: provide SOC2/ISO pack, provision VPC sandbox with store=false and demo dataset, follow up pilot kickoff.

Topics: Console privacy toggles, API param store=false, PII redaction presets, ephemeral request storage, KV cache considerations, audit logs / telemetry, KMS & key rotation, deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated), cost tradeoffs for retaining request telemetry.

[00:00] Alyssa: alright hey everyone thanks for joining, uh i'll kick us off. This is Alyssa from Redwood, i'm the account lead, and with me is Diego our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Priya: good thanks, thanks for fitting us in, we've been — we're evaluating options for request storage and basically want to see how redaction and the toggles work in real scenarios.
[00:11] Evan: yeah and we'll want to try the store=false flow end to end with our sample dataset.
[00:15] Diego: perfect, that's what we built this sandbox for. Quick agenda: i'll show the console configurator, then a live sandbox call using the API params (store=false, redact=pii-presets), then we'll look at the audit logs and KMS hookup.
[00:30] Marta: just to flag compliance - we need to understand audit log retention and whether logs contain any user-identifiable strings, like user ids in prompts.
[00:37] Diego: totally — we'll surface exactly where telemetry is written and how to scrub it. there are three layers: 1) request storage (full request + response), 2) telemetry/metrics with token-level cost/latency, and 3) audit logs for control plane events. you can toggle persistent storage off and still get ephemeral telemetry for SLOs.
[00:50] Alyssa: also shielding: we have redaction presets — like pii-basic, pii-strict, and custom regex. we'll demo pii-strict today which will remove ssn, passport, and email-like tokens by default.

[01:05] Diego: okay jumping into the console — sorry i know some of the names in the UI show as Redwood Optima in my recording, that's an earlier internal name — ignore that. so here is the privacy configurator page, top-level toggle: 'Persist requests' with three states: Enabled / Ephemeral / Disabled.
[01:22] Priya: what's ephemeral vs disabled?
[01:25] Diego: ephemeral means we keep request context only in-memory on the serving node for the duration of the inference and for short-lived batching needs; nothing is written to long-term object store. Disabled (store=false) means we do not keep the request or response payload at all — logs are limited to aggregated metrics and trace ids.
[01:42] Tom: so ephemeral would still let us do debugging if something fails?
[01:45] Diego: yes ephemeral can be configured to persist for X minutes for debugging, but it's not persisted to durable storage unless you flip it to Enabled.
[01:53] Evan: how does ephemeral interact with caching / KV cache? we rely on KV caches for context windows across prompt chains.
[01:59] Diego: good question — KV cache entries may reference tokenized prefix fragments; we have a policy to not persist full raw prompts if you set store=false. KV cache can be either in-memory only (for ephemeral) or backed to encrypted object store for enabled. and we can scrub caches during save.

[02:18] Marta: what about audit logs — who can see them and do they include prompt text?
[02:22] Diego: control-plane audit logs capture actions like model deployments, policy changes, and auth events. request-level audit can be enabled separately — by default control-plane logs do not include full prompts. if you need request-level logging for debugging or for compliance, that is opt-in and you can configure redaction rules.
[02:36] Priya: ok can you show the API side — we have microservices calling the API directly, we want to add a store flag per request.
[02:41] Diego: sure, here's a quick curl:
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-4k","input":"Summarize order 12345: ...","options":{"store_request":false,"redaction":"pii-strict"}}'

[03:05] Evan: so that options.store_request is honored even on hosted plan?
[03:08] Diego: yes, the hosted API honors per-request flags but there are some limits for retention analytics — on free tiers we keep minimal telemetry, on enterprise we can make it a hard guarantee via SLA and dedicated capacity.
[03:19] Priya: encryption for stored requests - is it customer-managed keys?
[03:23] Diego: on Private and Dedicated we offer KMS integration (bring-your-own-key) — you can enable CMEK for the object store that holds persisted request payloads. for hosted we use Redwood-managed keys by default but can set up key escrow for enterprise accounts.
[03:36] Marta: how does key rotation affect existing data? do we re-encrypt or keep old keys?
[03:40] Diego: typical KMS flows — rotate keys and re-encrypt on a schedule; we also support envelope encryption so rotated keys wrap a data key; re-encryption happens per your policy. we'll send the KMS whitepaper in the follow-up.

[03:55] Alyssa: Diego can you demo the console change so they can see the immediate behaviors?
[03:58] Diego: yep, toggling to Disabled (store=false) now. note the console warns: 'Analytics will be aggregated only; full transcripts won't be stored.' okay saved. the UI also shows a preview of what gets scrubbed — sample prompt with emails replaced by <REDACTED_EMAIL>.
[04:16] Priya: neat, can you customize the regexes?
[04:18] Diego: yes custom redaction rules — we have a test sandbox to upload 10 sample prompts and run the redaction preview. i'll run that now with a sample order text.
[04:30] [Screenshot shared: redaction preview showing masked credit card, email, phone]
[04:34] Evan: looks good — but in our flows we enrich prompts with internal ids, we need to ensure those ids aren't stored even if they look like tokens. can we blacklist certain regex patterns?
[04:44] Diego: absolutely, you can add blacklist patterns per-tenant, even hashed identifiers, and we can apply hashing at ingest so the raw identifier never lands in storage.
[04:53] Priya: what's the impact on model outputs if we hash/anonymize identifiers? will the model still link context?
[04:58] Diego: for token-level context linking you might lose cross-request identity; if you need linking but not raw values, you can use deterministic hashing so the same id maps to the same token. that preserves correlation but obfuscates raw values.

[05:14] Marta: can we get SAML/SSO controls for who can flip these toggles? we need RBAC so only compliance and platform ops can change storage policy.
[05:21] Diego: yes RBAC in Console: roles include Admin, Platform, Compliance, Developer. toggles are behind a permission. all changes are audit-logged and can be forwarded to your SIEM via webhook or syslog.
[05:33] Priya: about forwarding logs — does forwarded LR/ logs ever contain prompt text?
[05:36] Diego: we recommend forwarding control-plane logs only; if you need request-level logs forwarded you must enable redaction first. the forwarder has a transforms stage that can strip or hash fields.

[05:52] Alyssa: quick pricing note — disabling storage reduces your per-request storage cost but may increase debugging time; we include a cost/visibility dashboard so you can see unit economics.
[06:02] Evan: any implications for latency? if we do ephemeral and in-memory caching, does that increase memory footprint and affect tail latency?
[06:08] Diego: ephemeral KV cache is in-process and actually reduces tail latency vs hitting object store; the tradeoff is memory pressure which we manage with LRU eviction and configurable cache size. on Dedicated you can increase the memory allocation.

[06:27] Priya: can we see the live API demo now with store=false?
[06:30] Diego: yep moving to the sandbox. i'm calling the sandbox endpoint with the options payload — okay response 200, returned summary but request not stored. i'll show the audit trace id 0x7f9a... use that id to request debug info — because store=false there's limited debug info, but ephemeral logs show the trace for 15 minutes.
[06:48] Tom: and if we need deeper debugging we flip ephemeral to persisted for a short window?
[06:52] Diego: correct — you can temporarily enable persistence for a timeboxed window and we keep it for X hours.

[07:00] [07:00-22:00 aggregate: Diego runs a few variations, shows redaction preview and some mis-typed tokens in transcript; customers ask specific edge cases]

[22:05] Evan: what about embeddings and vector stores — we frequently embed PII, do embeddings count as stored requests?
[22:12] Diego: embeddings are configurable; by default embeddings are stored in your project vector store. you can opt into ephemeral embeddings where the vector is kept in memory for session length and never persisted. also you can apply local projection/hashing before sending embeddings.
[22:28] Priya: do you offer server-side tokenization so we can obfuscate before sending?
[22:33] Diego: we have a preprocessing hook in Dedicated/Private modes — you can run a preprocessor that masks or hashes tokens before they leave your network. for hosted we provide client-side SDK helpers for masking.

[22:50] Marta: auditability requirement: we need proof that redaction happened (for auditors). do you produce attestations or hash digests of original content so we can prove the redaction step executed?
[22:59] Diego: we can produce an evidence log — a signed hash of the preprocessed payload and the redaction policy id. the signed attestation does not contain the raw content but proves the action. that's part of our enterprise compliance offering.

[23:20] Priya: any known gaps in regulatory regimes — like GDPR right to be forgotten? if a user asks deletion, how do we ensure it is fully removed from backups and traces?
[23:29] Diego: DR flows: we maintain deletion queues; when a deletion is requested we scrub persisted store and schedule re-encryption/replacement in backups. for hosted customers we give a deletion receipt. for on-prem we recommend integrating with your backup lifecycle.

[23:45] Evan: curious about observability — if we disable store, can we still get sampling metrics for model regression alerts?

[23:52] Diego: yes we have configurable sampling: you can retain 0.1% of requests for quality evals or sample by route/token patterns. sampling can be routed to a dedicated bucket and is covered by RBAC and redaction rules. this keeps you compliant but preserves minimal eval capability.

[24:15] Alyssa: can we discuss timelines — what would a pilot look like?
[24:19] Priya: pilot needs to test store=false across our nightly batch, and ensure embeddings not stored, and verify attestation flows. timeline two to four weeks.
[24:26] Alyssa: ok we'll aim to have the sandbox by next week and pilot kickoff the week after.

[24:35] Diego: one more detail — request metadata: we still capture non-identifying metadata like model version, token counts, latency buckets. those help with cost analysis and do not contain prompt text unless you enable request logging.
[24:49] Marta: any retention defaults for audit logs?
[24:52] Diego: control-plane audit logs default 90 days; enterprise customers can extend to custom durations and use their own log export.

[25:05] Evan: competitor question — we evaluated Anthropic and they have a similar per-request flag but they limit per-minute toggles; how is Redwood different?
[25:13] Alyssa: we allow per-request toggles at scale and also offer deterministic hashing + KMS integration across deployment modes; we also expose cost/latency breakdown so ops can balance visibility vs cost.

[25:30] Priya: risk scenarios — say a dev accidentally flips Enabled on prod, is there guardrail?
[25:34] Diego: yes you can require approvals for toggle changes via two-person approval or policy checks — console will also show a change diff and send email/SOAR trigger.

[25:48] Tom: technical deep dive request — Evan and Diego to sync on KV cache behavior with anonymized ids.
[25:53] Evan: yes, let's set that up, i'll send my cache traces.

[26:00] Diego: noting that down — also for embedding privacy, we recommend client-side projection where possible.

[26:12] [26:12-37:00 Diego shows more demos, transcript contains some mis-heard words, e.g., 'optima', 'kv cache' sometimes 'k v cash']

[37:05] Marta: earlier you mentioned an attestation flow — can you send an example artifact we can show auditors?
[37:11] Diego: yes i'll include a sample signed JSON-LD attestation plus the KMS rotation proof and a short whitepaper.

[37:22] Alyssa: i'll also attach our SOC2 + ISO summary and the standard DPA and data processing addendum.

[37:30] Priya: one more question — onboarding path: we want to start with hosted sandbox then evaluate Dedicated. what are the hooks to lift to Dedicated without huge migration work?
[37:40] Diego: the platform's deployment abstraction decouples policy and model versioning. to migrate we snapshot your config and routing rules, and we can port your KV cache strategy. Dedicated gives you CMEK and private networking. we'll provide a migration checklist.

[38:00] Evan: any perf implications for store=false on throughput?
[38:04] Diego: throughput is usually higher when not persisting to object store; the main tradeoff is memory and possibly increased CPU for on-the-fly redaction. but overall we see similar or better throughput.

[38:20] Alyssa: ok wrapping up — recap and next steps.
[38:24] Alyssa: action items: Alyssa share SOC2/ISO and pricing; Diego provision sandbox and attestation sample; Novara to share sample prompts and retention policy. pilot kickoff week of 4/25.
[38:37] Priya: that's good. please include a short checklist for auditors.
[38:41] Diego: will do.
[38:45] Marta: thanks everyone, this was useful, appreciate the attestation detail.
[38:48] Alyssa: great, thanks all — we'll follow up over email and invite you to the sandbox.
[38:52] [End: informal wrap, small talk about lunch options, recording stops]

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-heard tokens (e.g., 'Redwood Optima' vs 'Redwood Optimize') and speaker overlaps. Shared artifacts: console-demo-recording-link: https://redwood.app/recordings/ff-20280411-demo-priv-config, sandbox-invite: https://redwood.app/sandbox/novara-ff-20280411
